title: ICC issues arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova over deportation of Ukrainian children
body:
On 17 March 2023 Pre-Trial Chamber II of the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Russian President Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, Russia's Presidential Commissioner for Children's Rights. Both are accused of the war crimes of unlawful deportation of population and unlawful transfer of population, concerning children moved from occupied areas of Ukraine to the Russian Federation. Putin is also accused on the basis of superior responsibility, for failing to control subordinates who committed or allowed the acts.

The chamber agreed with the prosecution's application of February 2023 and found reasonable grounds to believe that both individuals bear individual criminal responsibility. The alleged crimes date from at least 24 February 2022, the start of the full-scale invasion. These were the first ICC warrants connected with the war in Ukraine.

The warrants were initially sealed to protect victims, witnesses and the investigation. The court made their existence public in the interests of justice, citing that public awareness of the warrants may contribute to the prevention of the further commission of crimes. The ICC has no police force and relies on member states to carry out arrests. Russia withdrew from the ICC in 2016 and does not recognise its jurisdiction, according to Lawfare's account of the announcement.
